findings.problem: The receivers don't match. IsEmpty uses a pointer receiver and is nil-safe, but SupportsLevel (line 48) and SupportsOperator (line 56) use value receivers. SearchCapabilities.Filter is a *FilterCapabilities, so the natural call `caps.Filter.SupportsOperator(op)` panics with a nil dereference when a reader leaves Filter nil, which the docs describe as the normal 'no filter support' case. The doc says a nil Filter means the same as an empty one, but only IsEmpty behaves that way.
findings.fix: Make Filter a plain value (see the search_capabilities.go:28 finding) and give all three methods value receivers. If the pointer is kept, give SupportsLevel and SupportsOperator pointer receivers that treat nil as the zero value (`c == nil` → `level == ""` and `false`), and add nil-receiver cases to filter_test.go.

findings.problem: `Filter *FilterCapabilities` has two encodings for one state: nil and &FilterCapabilities{} both mean 'no filter support'. The docs then have to tell every caller to use IsEmpty instead of comparing against nil. The pointer adds no information, and it makes `assert.Equal` on forwarded SearchCapabilities depend on which encoding was used. It also clashes with the type's own rule that the zero value is the least capable reader.
findings.fix: Change the field to `Filter FilterCapabilities`, drop the nil case from the doc comments here and on FilterCapabilities (filter.go:28-30, 41-42), switch IsEmpty to a value receiver, and remove the nil case from TestFilterCapabilities_IsEmpty.

findings.problem: The field-count guard doesn't do its job. The count is already 3, but TestReadMetricsDecorator_SearchCapabilities (tracestoremetrics/reader_metrics_test.go:265-268) only covers WithoutServiceName and never sets SameSpanConjunction or Filter, so the guard passed while the table was never extended. The comment also points to a queryinterceptor test that is not in this package. Forwarding returns the whole struct (reader_metrics.go:134), so listing every field case by case adds nothing.
findings.fix: Delete TestSearchCapabilities_FieldCount. Replace the decorator's case table with a single case where every field is non-zero, e.g. `{WithoutServiceName: true, SameSpanConjunction: true, Filter: FilterCapabilities{Levels: []expression.Level{expression.LevelSpan}, Operators: []expression.Operator{expression.OpAnd}}}`, plus the zero value. Also add a case where the inner reader returns an error wrapping errors.ErrUnsupported, and check that the error is forwarded.

findings.problem: SearchCapabilities was inserted between GetServices and its doc comment. `// GetServices implements tracestore.Reader#GetServices` now sits above the SearchCapabilities comment block, so godoc attaches it to the wrong method and GetServices has no doc.
findings.fix: Move the `// GetServices implements tracestore.Reader#GetServices` line to just above `func (m *ReadMetricsDecorator) GetServices`, and keep SearchCapabilities' own two-line comment directly above it.

findings.problem: The FindTraces doc still says there is an 'implementation-dependent ambiguity' about whether conjunctive filters must match the same span. SearchCapabilities.SameSpanConjunction now settles that per reader. The doc also says nothing about the new Filter field or the errors a reader must return for it: ErrFilterUnsupported and ErrFilterInvalid are declared in filter.go but nothing in the Reader contract refers to them.
findings.fix: Replace the ambiguity paragraph with: whether a conjunction is satisfied within a single span is declared by SearchCapabilities().SameSpanConjunction. Then add: a reader given a Filter beyond its SearchCapabilities().Filter returns an error wrapping ErrFilterUnsupported, and one given a value that does not fit its field returns an error wrapping ErrFilterInvalid. Point FindTraceIDs and FindTraceSummaries at this rule.

findings.problem: The comment says Filter is mutually exclusive with the predicate fields, but nothing in the package enforces that or says what a reader does when both are set. Every backend has to re-implement the check, or skip it, and in practice the check will drift between backends.
findings.fix: Add a `func (p TraceQueryParams) Validate() error` (or a narrower `checkFilterExclusive`) to reader.go. It returns an error wrapping ErrFilterInvalid when Filter != nil and any of ServiceName, OperationName, Attributes.Len() > 0, DurationMin or DurationMax is set. Document in FindTraces that readers call it, and test it in reader_test.go, which is currently empty.
